figures.alt: Photograph of Villa Rotonda seen from the lawn: a square villa with a domed roof and a pedimented Ionic portico of six columns above a wide flight of steps, with statues on the pediment.
figures.caption: Fig. 1. Villa Rotonda, near Vicenza. Photo: the author.

figures.alt: Photograph of the street façade of Palazzo Porto in Vicenza, seen at an angle: a rusticated ground floor and an upper floor with Ionic half-columns, balconied windows and pediments.
figures.caption: Fig. 2. Vicenza, Palazzo Porto. Photo: the author.

figures.alt: Photograph of the front of Villa Cornaro: a two-storey portico of Ionic and Corinthian columns crowned by a pediment, between plain side wings, reached by a broad flight of steps.
figures.caption: Fig. 3. Piombino Dese, Villa Cornaro. Photo: the author.

figures.alt: Photograph of the nave of San Giorgio Maggiore looking towards the altar: tall white columns and pilasters, arches and barrel vaults, with a crucifix and the choir beyond.
figures.caption: Fig. 4. Venice, San Giorgio Maggiore. Photo: the author.

figures.alt: Plate from the Quattro libri showing the five orders in sequence, as colonnades and as arcades, drawn in elevation with plans of the column bases below.
figures.caption: Fig. 5. The architectural orders as presented in the Quattro libri.
figures.credit: A. Palladio, I quattro libri dell'architettura (1570), public domain

figures.alt: Two architectural sections compared: above, the longitudinal section of San Giorgio Maggiore with its dome; below, the section of the frigidarium of the Baths of Diocletian with three large arches.
figures.caption: Fig. 6. Top: Section of San Giorgio Maggiore (from Cicognara, Diedo & Selva 1815-1820); and bottom: Longitudinal section of the frigidarium of the Baths of Diocletian (from a drawing by Andrea Palladio: London, R.I.B.A., Palladio V, 2. Source: London, Courtauld Institute).
figures.credit: Cicognara, Diedo & Selva (1815–1820); A. Palladio drawing, RIBA, London (source: Courtauld Institute)

figures.alt: Woodcut from the Quattro libri: plan of Villa Rotonda with a circular central hall and four porticoes, and below it a half elevation and half section showing the dome.
figures.caption: Fig. 7. Villa Rotonda as illustrated in the Quattro libri, libro II, p. 19.
figures.credit: A. Palladio, I quattro libri dell'architettura (1570), public domain

figures.alt: Geometric diagram of Villa Rotonda: the plan and section overlaid with concentric circles, diagonals and construction lines.
figures.caption: Fig. 8. Analytical diagram of Villa Rotonda by Robert Streitz.

figures.alt: Photograph of the Victoria Shopping Centre in Harrogate: a curved two-storey arcaded façade in stone with a glazed roof, modelled on the Basilica in Vicenza.
figures.caption: Fig. 9. Harrogate, Victoria Shopping Centre, designed by Cullearn & Phillips, completed 1991. Photo: Derek Harper, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).
figures.credit: Photo: Derek Harper, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

figures.alt: Photograph of Schulhaus Im Birch in Zürich: a four-storey modern school building with a grid of horizontal windows and a paved square with trees in front.
figures.caption: Fig. 10. Zürich, Schulhaus Im Birch, designed by Peter Märkli, 2004. Photo: Tschubby, Wikimedia Commons, File: Schulhaus Im Birch 2019.
